nodes.label: desktop memory - hard fields materialized before tagging

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. The user's intended HERB architecture: structured hard fields extracted from source records - product, section, channel, employee_id, dates, ids - are materialized as first-class, indexed, queryable :Chunk properties in a stage that runs BEFORE tagging, so retrieval can act on them deterministically before any tag or embedding step. The shipped graph at the time did not do this: hard fields sat only inside Chunk.content, a verbatim blob, and Chunk.locator_json, a provenance string, neither of them searchable, so a prompt about a literal that was never tagged could not retrieve the chunk containing it and recall was capped by tagger coverage rather than corpus content. The entry carries two dated updates in place: CONFIRMED as the carrier 2026-06-12, where the v2 graph-spine decision lands exactly here and hard fields are indexed chunk attributes rather than entity nodes or edges; and SUPERSEDED on the retrieval-gate point, where hard fields participate in retrieval as soft boosts and never gates, with true exact-match living on the separate structured-query and aggregation path. The materialization stance is unchanged and load-bearing; only the retrieval-time use changed from gate to boost
